claim: CDG elicits stronger Ab responses than 2′3′-cGAMP in mice.
source: Here, we showed, in mice, that CDG elicits stronger Ab and TH responses than the mammalian 2′3′-cyclic GMP-AMP (cGAMP)
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing higher anti-OVA IgG1 and IgA production in CDG adjuvanted vaccine compared to 2′3′-cGAMP adjuvanted vaccine (Figure 1A).

claim: CDG elicits stronger TH responses than 2′3′-cGAMP in mice.
source: Here, we showed, in mice, that CDG elicits stronger Ab and TH responses than the mammalian 2′3′-cyclic GMP-AMP (cGAMP)
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing higher IL-13 and IL-17 production in CDG adjuvanted vaccine compared to 2′3′-cGAMP adjuvanted vaccine (Figure 1B).

claim: CDG adjuvanted vaccine generates better protection against Streptococcus pneumoniae infection than 2′3′-cGAMP adjuvanted vaccine.
source: Here, we showed, in mice, that CDG elicits stronger Ab and TH responses than the mammalian 2′3′-cyclic GMP-AMP (cGAMP), and generated better protection against Streptococcus pneumoniae infection than 2′3′-cGAMP adjuvanted vaccine.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing lower bacterial burden in lungs and spleens of CDG/PspA immunized mice compared to 2′3′-cGAMP/PspA immunized mice (Figure 1E).

claim: Intranasally administered CDG greatly enhances Ag uptake in vivo.
source: First, intranasally administered CDG greatly enhances Ag uptake, including pinocytosis and receptor-mediated endocytosis in vivo.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing dramatically increased numbers of OVA-647+ cells in lungs after CDG treatment (Figure 4C).

claim: CDG enhancement of Ag uptake includes both pinocytosis and receptor-mediated endocytosis.
source: First, intranasally administered CDG greatly enhances Ag uptake, including pinocytosis and receptor-mediated endocytosis in vivo.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing both OVA-647hi cells (receptor-mediated endocytosis) and OVA-647low cells (pinocytosis) after CDG treatment (Figure 4F).

claim: The enhancement of Ag uptake by CDG depends on MPYS expression in CD11C+ cells.
source: The enhancement depends on MPYS (STING, MITA) expression in CD11C+ cells.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing dramatically decreased DQ+ cells in ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice (Figure 8A,B).

claim: CDG selectively activates pinocytosis-efficient-DCs in vivo.
source: Second, we found that CDG selectively activated pinocytosis-efficient-DCs, leading to TH polarizing cytokines IL-12p70, IFNγ, IL-5, IL-13, IL-23, and IL-6 production in vivo.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing that only DQ-Green+DQ-Red−CD86+ cells (pinocytosis-efficient DCs) were activated and migratory (Figures 5F, 6B,E).

claim: CDG activated pinocytosis-efficient-DCs produce TH polarizing cytokines IL-12p70, IFNγ, IL-5, IL-13, IL-23, and IL-6 in vivo.
source: Second, we found that CDG selectively activated pinocytosis-efficient-DCs, leading to TH polarizing cytokines IL-12p70, IFNγ, IL-5, IL-13, IL-23, and IL-6 production in vivo.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing production of these cytokines in lungs after CDG treatment (Figure 3B-D).

claim: CDG induces IFNλ in vivo.
source: Notably, CDG induces IFNλ, but not IFNβ, in vivo.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing potent IFNλ production in lungs after CDG treatment (Figure 3A).

claim: CDG does not induce IFNβ in vivo.
source: Notably, CDG induces IFNλ, but not IFNβ, in vivo.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing no increase in IFNβ levels above background after CDG treatment (Figure 3A).

claim: CDG is a promising mucosal vaccine adjuvant.
source: Cyclic di-GMP (CDG) is a promising mucosal vaccine adjuvant candidate (Ogunniyi et al., 2008; Hu et al., 2009; Chen et al., 2010; Madhun et al., 2011; Gray et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies demonstrating CDG's adjuvant properties.

claim: CDG is ubiquitously found in bacteria but is absent in higher eukaryotes.
source: It is ubiquitously found in bacteria, but is absent in higher eukaryotes.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about the distribution of cyclic di-GMP.

claim: Intranasal administration of CDG with PsaA elicits comparable Ag-specific Ab response to cholera toxin with PsaA.
source: Yan et al. found that intranasal administration of CDG, along with the pneumococcal Ag PsaA, elicits a comparable Ag-specific Ab response, and reduces bacterial colonization to those mice immunized with cholera toxin and PsaA (Yan et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Yan et al., 2009 study.

claim: Cholera toxin is the most potent experimental mucosal adjuvant.
source: Cholera toxin is the most potent experimental mucosal adjuvant.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge in the field of mucosal immunology.

claim: CDG exhibits balanced TH1, TH2, and TH17 immune responses.
source: CDG also exhibits balanced TH1, TH2, and TH17 immune responses (Ebensen et al., 2007, 2011; Gray et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies (Ebensen et al., 2007, 2011; Gray et al., 2012).

claim: CDG is a more potent activator of both TH1 and TH2 immune responses than LPS, CpG oligonucleotides, and aluminum salt based adjuvant in mice.
source: A recent study found that CDG is a more potent activator of both TH1 and TH2 immune responses than LPS, CpG oligonucleotides (ODN), and aluminum salt based adjuvant in mice (Gray et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Gray et al., 2012 study.

claim: MPYS-deficient mice completely lost CDG induced Ag-specific Ab and TH responses.
source: We previously showed that MPYS-deficient mice (Tmem173−/−) completely lost CDG induced Ag-specific Ab and TH responses (Blaauboer et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work by the authors (Blaauboer et al., 2014).

claim: MPYS is also known as STING, MITA, and TMEM173.
source: MPYS, also known as STING, MITA, and TMEM173, is a type I IFN stimulator (Ishikawa and Barber, 2008; Jin et al., 2008; Zhong et al., 2008).
evidence: Based on established nomenclature in the field, supported by citations.

claim: Type I IFN signaling is not required for the mucosal adjuvant activity of CDG in vivo.
source: However, we found that type I IFN signaling is not required for the mucosal adjuvant activity of CDG in vivo (Blaauboer et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work by the authors (Blaauboer et al., 2014).

claim: CDG activates both type I IFN and NF-κB signaling.
source: CDG activates both type I IFN and NF-κB signaling (McWhirter et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to McWhirter et al., 2009 study.

claim: MPYS is required for both CDG induced type I IFN and NF-κB activations.
source: While MPYS is required for both CDG induced type I IFN and NF-κB activations (Jin et al., 2011a; Sauer et al., 2011), we found that these two pathways can be uncoupled in dendritic cells (DCs) and macrophages (Blaauboer et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Jin et al., 2011a; Sauer et al., 2011; and Blaauboer et al., 2014.

claim: Type I IFN and NF-κB pathways can be uncoupled in dendritic cells and macrophages.
source: While MPYS is required for both CDG induced type I IFN and NF-κB activations (Jin et al., 2011a; Sauer et al., 2011), we found that these two pathways can be uncoupled in dendritic cells (DCs) and macrophages (Blaauboer et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work by the authors (Blaauboer et al., 2014).

claim: 2′3′-cGAMP is a newly discovered mammalian cyclic dinucleotide that has mucosal adjuvant activity in vivo.
source: The 2′3′-cyclic GMP-AMP (cGAMP) is a newly discovered mammalian cyclic dinucleotide that also has mucosal adjuvant activity in vivo (Skrnjug et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Skrnjug et al., 2014 study.

claim: Both CDG and 2′3′-cGAMP can bind MPYS in vitro.
source: Both CDG and 2′3′-cGAMP can bind MPYS in vitro (Burdette et al., 2011; Gao et al., 2013a; Sun et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to Burdette et al., 2011; Gao et al., 2013a; Sun et al., 2013.

claim: 2′3′-cGAMP has a much better binding affinity to MPYS than CDG.
source: The 2′3′-cGAMP has a much better binding affinity to MPYS than CDG (Gao et al., 2013c).
evidence: Supported by citation to Gao et al., 2013c study.

claim: 2′3′-cGAMP induces stronger type I IFN production than CDG in mammalian cells.
source: Furthermore, 2′3′-cGAMP induces stronger type I IFN production than CDG does in mammalian cells (Gao et al., 2013c).
evidence: Supported by citation to Gao et al., 2013c study.

claim: CDG adjuvanted vaccine induced higher Ag-specific IgG1 and IgA production than 2′3′-cGAMP adjuvanted vaccine in BALB/c mice.
source: Surprisingly, CDG adjuvanted vaccine induced higher Ag-specific IgG1 and IgA production than the 2′3′-cGAMP adjuvanted vaccine (Figure 1A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The production of OVA-specific IgG2A was similar in both CDG and 2′3′-cGAMP vaccines in BALB/c mice.
source: The production of OVA-specific IgG2A was similar in both vaccines (Figure 1A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: CDG adjuvanted vaccine generated better IL-13 and IL-17 production than 2′3′-cGAMP adjuvanted vaccine in BALB/c mice.
source: Again, CDG adjuvanted vaccine generated better IL-13, a TH2 cytokine, and IL-17 production than the 2′3′-cGAMP adjuvanted vaccine (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The TH1 cytokine IFNγ was similarly produced by both CDG and 2′3′-cGAMP in BALB/c mice.
source: The TH1 cytokine, IFNγ, was similarly produced by both cyclic dinucleotides (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: CDG adjuvanted PspA based pneumococcal vaccine generated higher titers of PspA-specific IgG1 and nasal IgA in C57BL/6 mice.
source: We found that CDG adjuvanted PspA based pneumococcal vaccine generated higher titers of PspA-specific IgG1 and nasal IgA (Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: CDG adjuvanted pneumococcal vaccine had stronger IL-13 and IL-17 responses than 2′3′-cGAMP adjuvanted pneumococcal vaccine in C57BL/6 mice.
source: Additionally, they had stronger IL-13 (TH2) and IL-17 (TH17) responses in the ex vivo recall assay than the 2′3′-cGAMP adjuvanted pneumococcal vaccine (Figure 1D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The IgG2C and IFNγ responses were similar between CDG and 2′3′-cGAMP adjuvanted vaccine in C57BL/6 mice.
source: The IgG2C and IFNγ (TH1) responses were similar between CDG and 2′3′-cGAMP adjuvanted vaccine (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1C and 1D.

claim: Mice immunized with CDG adjuvanted pneumococcal vaccine have lower bacterial burden in spleens and lungs than mice immunized with 2′3′-cGAMP adjuvanted pneumococcal vaccine.
source: We found that mice immunized with CDG adjuvanted pneumococcal vaccine have a lower bacterial burden in the spleens and lungs than mice immunized with 2′3′-cGAMP adjuvant pneumococcal vaccine (Figure 1E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: At 5 μg dose, CDG causes only very mild neutrophil infiltration in BALF and lungs.
source: At the dose of CDG used in Figure 1 (5 μg), we saw only very mild neutrophil infiltration in Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) (Figure 2A) and lungs (Figure 2D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2A and 2D.

claim: There was no significant difference in serum albumin level in BALF between saline and CDG treated mice.
source: There was no significant difference in samples from saline or CDG treated mice (Figure 2B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B measuring lung permeability.

claim: Lung histology did not reveal any lung damage in CDG treated mice.
source: Last, lung histology also did not reveal any lung damage in CDG treated mice (Figure 2C).
evidence: Supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Intranasally administered CDG at the dose used as an effective mucosal adjuvant did not cause lung injury.
source: We concluded that intranasally administered CDG, at the dose used as an effective mucosal adjuvant, did not cause lung injury.
evidence: Based on inference from experimental data showing no significant lung damage markers (Figures 2A-D).

claim: There was a ~twofold increase in Ly6Chi monocytes in the lung after intranasal CDG administration.
source: Besides a mild increase in the number of neutrophils in lung, there was also a ∼twofold increase in Ly6Chi monocytes in the lung after intranasal CDG administration (Figure 2D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: There were no significant increases in numbers of Mast cells or eosinophils in lungs at the vaccine adjuvant dose of CDG used (5 μg).
source: There were no significant increases in numbers of Mast cells or eosinophils in lungs at the vaccine adjuvant dose of CDG used (5 μg) (Figure 2D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: There were no increases in the number of B cells or NK cells after CDG treatment.
source: There were also no increases in the number of B cells or NK cells (Figure 2D,E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2D and 2E.

claim: There was no difference in total DC number, or CD103+, CD11B+ DCs subset numbers in the lungs after CDG treatment.
source: We did not find any difference in total DC number, or CD103+, CD11B+ DCs subset numbers in the lungs after CDG treatment (Figure 2F,G).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2F and 2G.

claim: CDG induces the production of proinflammatory cytokines TNFα and IL-1β in vivo.
source: CDG induces the production of the proinflammatory cytokines TNFα and IL-1β in vitro (Karaolis et al., 2007). We confirmed this in vivo (Figure 2H).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2H and citation to Karaolis et al., 2007.

claim: CDG induced potent IL-10 production in vivo.
source: However, we found that CDG also induced potent IL-10 production, an anti-inflammatory cytokine, in vivo (Figure 2I).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2I.

claim: CDG induced strong IL-22 production in vivo.
source: Furthermore, CDG induced strong IL-22 production in vivo (Figure 2I), which is important for lung epithelium repair (Paget et al., 2012; Pociask et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2I and citations to Paget et al., 2012; Pociask et al., 2013.

claim: CDG-induced TNFα and IL-22 production were completely dependent on the expression of MPYS.
source: While CDG-induced TNFα and IL-22 production were completely dependent on the expression of MPYS, IL-1β, and IL-10 production in vivo were only partially dependent on MPYS (Figure 2H,I).
evidence: Supported by experimental data comparing WT and Tmem173−/− mice shown in Figures 2H and 2I.

claim: CDG-induced IL-1β and IL-10 production in vivo were only partially dependent on MPYS.
source: While CDG-induced TNFα and IL-22 production were completely dependent on the expression of MPYS, IL-1β, and IL-10 production in vivo were only partially dependent on MPYS (Figure 2H,I).
evidence: Supported by experimental data comparing WT and Tmem173−/− mice shown in Figures 2H and 2I.

claim: CDG treatment did not increase IFNβ levels above background in the lungs.
source: Although we detected low-level background IFNβ production in the lungs, CDG treatment did not increase IFNβ levels above the background (Figure 3A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: CDG induced potent type III IFN (IFN λ) production in the lungs.
source: Surprisingly, we detected potent type III IFN (IFN λ) production in the lungs after intranasal administration of 5 μg CDG (Figure 3A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Type III IFN receptors are mainly expressed on lung epithelial cells.
source: Type III IFN activates similar groups of interferon stimulating genes (ISGs) as type I IFN. However, their receptors are mainly expressed on lung epithelial cells (Zhou et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zhou et al., 2007 study.

claim: Neutralizing IFNλ in vivo did not affect the adjuvant activity of CDG.
source: Furthermore, neutralizing IFNλ in vivo did not affect the adjuvant activity of CDG (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: CDG induced strong type II IFN (IFN γ) in vivo.
source: We also detected strong CDG induced type II IFN (IFN γ) in vivo (Figure 3B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Both type II and III IFN production by CDG were absent in MPYS−/− mice.
source: Both type II and III IFN production by CDG were absent in MPYS−/− mice (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data comparing WT and Tmem173−/− mice shown in Figures 3A and 3B.

claim: Intranasally administered CDG induces TH1 polarizing cytokine IL-12p70 in the lungs.
source: Indeed, intranasally administered CDG induced TH1 polarizing cytokine IL-12p70, TH2 polarizing cytokine IL-5, to a lesser degree IL-4 and IL-13, and TH17 polarizing cytokines IL-23, IL-6, and TGF-β1 (Figure 3B–D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3B-D.

claim: Intranasally administered CDG induces TH2 polarizing cytokines IL-5, IL-4, and IL-13 in the lungs.
source: Indeed, intranasally administered CDG induced TH1 polarizing cytokine IL-12p70, TH2 polarizing cytokine IL-5, to a lesser degree IL-4 and IL-13, and TH17 polarizing cytokines IL-23, IL-6, and TGF-β1 (Figure 3B–D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3B-D.

claim: Intranasally administered CDG induces TH17 polarizing cytokines IL-23, IL-6, and TGF-β1 in the lungs.
source: Indeed, intranasally administered CDG induced TH1 polarizing cytokine IL-12p70, TH2 polarizing cytokine IL-5, to a lesser degree IL-4 and IL-13, and TH17 polarizing cytokines IL-23, IL-6, and TGF-β1 (Figure 3B–D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3B-D.

claim: All CDG induced TH polarizing cytokines except IL-6 were absent in Tmem173−/− mice.
source: Except for IL-6 production, all these CDG induced cytokines were absent in Tmem173−/− mice (Figure 3B–3D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data comparing WT and Tmem173−/− mice shown in Figures 3B-3D.

claim: CDG induced potent IL-33 production in vivo.
source: Indeed, CDG induced potent IL-33 and, to a lesser degree, IL-1α and TSLP production (Figure 3E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: CDG induced IL-1α and TSLP production to a lesser degree than IL-33.
source: Indeed, CDG induced potent IL-33 and, to a lesser degree, IL-1α and TSLP production (Figure 3E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: CDG induced lung epithelium cytokines were only partially dependent on the expression of MPYS.
source: Distinct from many of the cytokines examined above, these CDG induced lung epithelium cytokines were only partially dependent on the expression of MPYS (Figure 3E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data comparing WT and Tmem173−/− mice shown in Figure 3E.

claim: All cytokines were detected at both 6 hr and 24 hr post CDG administration.
source: Noticeably, all cytokines were detected at both 6 hr and 24 hr post CDG administration (Figure 2 and Figure 3).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: CDG induced cytokines could be detected as early as 4 hr post CDG administration in vivo.
source: In fact, we could detect these cytokines as early as 4 hr post CDG administration in vivo.
evidence: Supported by experimental observations.

claim: IL-12p35+ DC accounted for ~0.035% of DCs in lungs from CDG treated mice.
source: IL-12p35+ DC accounted for ∼0.035% of DCs, which amounted to less than 500 of these cells in a lung from a CDG treated mouse (Figure 3G).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: The percentage of IL-12p35+ IFNγ+ DC was ~0.01%.
source: The percentage of IL-12p35+ IFNγ+ DC was ∼0.01% (Figure 3F,G).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3F and 3G.

claim: No IL-12p35+ DCs were detected in saline treated mice.
source: As a control, no IL-12p35+ DCs were detected in saline treated mice (Figure 3F).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: CDG dramatically improved Ag uptake as indicated by increased number of OVA-647+ cells in lung.
source: We found that including CDG in the immunization dramatically improved Ag uptake, as indicated by the increased number of OVA-647+ cells in lung (Figure 4C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: ~34% of OVA-647+ cells were DQ+, indicating that only a portion of OVA-647+ cells has the ability to process Ag.
source: Furthermore, ∼34% of these OVA-647+ cells were DQ+, which indicated that only a portion of OVA-647+ cells has the ability to process Ag (Figure 4C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The CDG induced OVA-647+ cells included both MHC II+ APCs and MHC II− non-APCs.
source: Of note, the CDG induced OVA-647+ cells included both MHC II+ APCs and MHC II− non-APCs (Figure 4C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: There are three populations of antigen presenting cells (APCs) from WT mice: MHC IIhiCD11C+, MHC IIlowCD11C+ and MHC IIintCD11C−.
source: There are three populations of antigen presenting cells (APCs) from WT mice: MHC IIhiCD11C+ (i.e., DCs), MHC IIlowCD11C+ and MHC IIintCD11C− (Figure 4D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The majority of OVA-647+MHC IIlowCD11C+ cells were OVA-647hi cells.
source: Notably, the majority of OVA-647+MHC IIlowCD11C+ cells were OVA-647hi cells, while the majority of OVA-647+MHC IIhiCD11C+ and OVA-647+ MHC IIintCD11C− cells were OVA-647low cells (Figure 4F).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The majority of OVA-647+MHC IIhiCD11C+ and OVA-647+ MHC IIintCD11C− cells were OVA-647low cells.
source: Notably, the majority of OVA-647+MHC IIlowCD11C+ cells were OVA-647hi cells, while the majority of OVA-647+MHC IIhiCD11C+ and OVA-647+ MHC IIintCD11C− cells were OVA-647low cells (Figure 4F).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: OVA-647hi cells were generated via receptor-mediated endocytosis while OVA-647low cells were a result of pinocytosis-mediated Ag uptake.
source: A previous study established that OVA-647hi cells were generated via receptor-mediated endocytosis while OVA-647low cells were a result of pinocytosis-mediated Ag uptake (Burgdorf et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citation to Burgdorf et al., 2007 study.

claim: CDG predominantly enhanced receptor-mediated endocytosis in MHC IIlowCD11C+ cells.
source: Thus, CDG predominantly enhanced receptor-mediated endocytosis in MHC IIlowCD11C+ and pinocytosis in MHC IIhiCD11C+ and MHC IIintCD11C− cells.
evidence: Based on inference from the observation that MHC IIlowCD11C+ cells were predominantly OVA-647hi (receptor-mediated endocytosis).

claim: CDG predominantly enhanced pinocytosis in MHC IIhiCD11C+ and MHC IIintCD11C− cells.
source: Thus, CDG predominantly enhanced receptor-mediated endocytosis in MHC IIlowCD11C+ and pinocytosis in MHC IIhiCD11C+ and MHC IIintCD11C− cells.
evidence: Based on inference from the observation that MHC IIhiCD11C+ and MHC IIintCD11C− cells were predominantly OVA-647low (pinocytosis).

claim: In the OVA-647+ MHC IIlowCD11C+ population, there was no increase of the activation marker CD86.
source: In the OVA-647+ MHC IIlowCD11C+ population, there was no increase of the activation marker CD86 (Figure 4E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: In MHC IIhiCD11C+ and MHC IIintCD11C− populations, the OVA-647+ cells had increased CD86 expression.
source: In the remaining two APC populations, MHC IIhiCD11C+ and MHC IIintCD11C−, the OVA-647+ cells had increased CD86 expression (Figure 4E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: CDG activates MHC IIhiCD11C+ and MHC IIintCD11C−, but not MHC IIlowCD11C+ APCs in vivo.
source: Thus, CDG activates MHC IIhiCD11C+ and MHC IIintCD11C−, but not MHC IIlowCD11C+ APCs in vivo.
evidence: Based on inference from CD86 expression data (Figure 4E).

claim: The total numbers of CD86+MHC IIhi activated OVA-647+ cells were similar between MHC IIhiCD11C+ and MHC IIintCD11C− APCs.
source: The total numbers of CD86+MHC IIhi activated OVA-647+ cells were similar between MHC IIhiCD11C+ and MHC IIintCD11C− APCs (Figure 4G).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Cell activation is not a prerequisite for CDG enhanced Ag uptake in vivo.
source: This suggested that cell activation is not a prerequisite for CDG enhanced Ag uptake in vivo.
evidence: Based on inference from the observation that CDG enhanced Ag uptake in all three APC populations but only activated two of them.

claim: CDG dramatically increased numbers of DQ+ cells in vivo.
source: CDG also dramatically increased numbers of DQ+ cells in vivo (Figure 5A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The vast majority of DQ+ cells (~94%) were OVA-647+ cells.
source: Gated on the DQ+ lung cells, we found that the vast majority of DQ+ cells (∼94%) were OVA-647+ cells (Figure 5A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The DQ+OVA+ consisted of two populations: OVA-647hi and OVA-647low cells.
source: The DQ+OVA+ consisted of two populations: OVA-647hi and OVA-647low cells (Figure 5A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The DQ+OVA-647hi cells had a strong DQ-Red signal, indicating that processed Ag concentration was high in these cells.
source: The DQ+OVA-647hi cells had a strong DQ-Red signal, indicating that processed Ag concentration was high in these cells (Figure 5B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The DQ+OVA-647low cells were DQ-Red negative, though they still processed Ag as they were DQ-Green+.
source: The DQ+OVA-647low cells were DQ-Red negative, though they still processed Ag as they were DQ-Green+ (Figure 5B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Receptor-mediated Ag endocytosis generates DQ-Green+DQ-Red+ cells.
source: Thus, the receptor-mediated Ag endocytosis generates DQ-Green+DQ-Red+ cells, while pinocytosis-mediated Ag uptake generates DQ-Green+DQ-Red− cells.
evidence: Based on inference from the correlation between OVA-647hi cells (receptor-mediated) and DQ-Red+ signal.

claim: Pinocytosis-mediated Ag uptake generates DQ-Green+DQ-Red− cells.
source: Thus, the receptor-mediated Ag endocytosis generates DQ-Green+DQ-Red+ cells, while pinocytosis-mediated Ag uptake generates DQ-Green+DQ-Red− cells.
evidence: Based on inference from the correlation between OVA-647low cells (pinocytosis) and DQ-Red− signal.

claim: The DQ+ cells were almost exclusively APCs (MHC II+ cells).
source: We found that the DQ+ cells were almost exclusively APCs (MHC II+ cells) (Figure 5C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The vast majority of the DQ+ lung cells (>90% of DQ+ cells) were MHC IIlowCD11C+ APC.
source: Furthermore, the vast majority of the DQ+ lung cells (>90% of DQ+ cells) were MHC IIlowCD11C+ APC (Figure 5C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The MHC IIhiCD11C+ and MHC IIint CD11C− APCs accounted for ~1% and 2% of DQ+ cells, respectively.
source: The MHC IIhiCD11C+ and MHC IIint CD11C− APCs accounted for ∼1% and 2% of DQ+ cells, respectively (Figure 5C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The MHC IIlowCD11C+DQ+ cells were Siglec F+ cells, which should be characterized as alveolar macrophages.
source: The MHC IIlowCD11C+DQ+ cells were Siglec F+ (Figure 5C) cells, which should be characterized as alveolar macrophages.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C and knowledge of alveolar macrophage markers.

claim: Alveolar macrophages are the dominant Ag uptake and processing cells during intranasal CDG administration.
source: This suggested that alveolar macrophages are the dominant Ag uptake and processing cells during intranasal CDG administration.
evidence: Based on inference from the observation that >90% of DQ+ cells were alveolar macrophages.

claim: ~26% of total lung Siglec F+ alveolar macrophages were DQ+ cells.
source: Indeed, ∼26% of total lung Siglec F+ alveolar macrophages were DQ+ cells (Figure 5D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Only ~1% of total lung cells were DQ+ cells.
source: In comparison, only ∼1% of total lung cells were DQ+ cells (Figure 5A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The only CD86+ APC among DQ+ cells was MHC IIhi DCs.
source: However, in DQ+ cells, the only CD86+ APC was MHC IIhi DCs (Figure 5E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: CD86+ DQ+ MHC IIhi DCs also had increased CD80 expression.
source: These cells also had increased CD80 expression (Figure 5E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: OVA-647low cells were all DQ-Red− while OVA-647hi cells were all DQ-Red+.
source: We found that OVA-647low cells were all DQ-Red− while OVA-647hi cells were all DQ-Red+ (Figure 5B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The vast majority of MHC IIhiCD86+CD80+DQ+ cells were DQ-Red− cells.
source: Similarly, the vast majority of MHC IIhiCD86+CD80+DQ+ cells were DQ-Red− cells (Figure 5F).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: During intranasal administration of CDG, the only APCs that took up Ag, processed Ag and activated, were MHC IIhi pinocytosis-efficient DCs.
source: We concluded that during intranasal administration of CDG, the only APCs that took up Ag (OVA-647+), processed Ag (DQ-Green+) and activated (CD86+CD80+), were MHC IIhi pinocytosis-efficient (DQ-Red−) DCs.
evidence: Based on inference from multiple experimental observations about Ag uptake, processing, and activation markers.

claim: CDG is a 690 Da small molecule with two phosphate groups that cannot directly cross cell membrane.
source: CDG is a 690 Da small molecule with two phosphate groups that cannot directly cross cell membrane (McWhirter et al., 2009; Chen et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to McWhirter et al., 2009; Chen et al., 2010 and knowledge of molecular properties.

claim: During intranasal administration, CDG is likely brought into the cytosol by pinocytosis.
source: Thus, during intranasal administration, CDG is likely brought into the cytosol by pinocytosis, and stimulates DCs.
evidence: Based on inference from CDG's inability to cross membranes and the observation that pinocytosis-efficient cells are activated.

claim: CDG enhanced Ag uptake and processing in both CD103+ and CD11B+ DCs.
source: By co-administration of DQ-OVA and CDG, we found that CDG enhanced Ag uptake and processing, as indicated by increased numbers of DQ+ cells, in both CD103+ and CD11B+ DCs (Figure 6A,D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figures 6A and 6D.

claim: CD103+DCs had a higher percentage of DQ+ cells than the CD11B+ DCs.
source: We did notice that CD103+DCs had a higher percentage of DQ+ cells than the CD11B+ DCs (Figure 6A,D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figures 6A and 6D.

claim: Both CD103+ and CD11B+ DC subsets had DQ-Red+ and DQ-Red− populations.
source: Both DC subsets had DQ-Red+ and DQ-Red− populations (Figure 6A,D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figures 6A and 6D.

claim: A significant portion of lung CD103+DQ+ DCs (~35%) from CDG treated mice were MHC IIhiCD86+ activated DCs.
source: A significant portion of lung CD103+DQ+ DCs (∼35%) from CDG treated mice were MHC IIhiCD86+ activated DCs (Figure 6B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: All activated DQ+CD103+CD86+ DCs were DQ-Red negative cells.
source: Interestingly, these activated DQ+CD103+CD86+ DCs were all DQ-Red negative cells (Figure 6B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: All DQ-Red− CD103+ cells were CD86+ DCs and all DQ-Red+ CD103+ cells were CD86−.
source: In fact, it appeared that all DQ-Red− cells were CD86+ DCs and all DQ-Red+ cells were CD86− (Figure 6B,C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figures 6B and 6C.

claim: CDG treatment increased total CD103+ DCs numbers in DLN.
source: CDG treatment increased total CD103+ DCs numbers in DLN (Figure 6H,L).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figures 6H and 6L.

claim: Only a very small percentage of the migratory CD103+ DCs (~1.8%) were DQ+.
source: However, only a very small percentage of the migratory CD103+ DCs (∼1.8%) were DQ+ (Figure 6H,M).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figures 6H and 6M.

claim: A large portion of CD103+ DCs were migratory, likely activated by CDG, but did not take up the DQ-OVA Ag.
source: This indicated that a large portion of CD103+ DCs were migratory, likely activated by CDG, but did not take up the DQ-OVA Ag.
evidence: Based on inference from the observation that total CD103+ DCs increased but only a small percentage were DQ+.

claim: The vast majority of DQ+CD103+ migratory DCs were MHC IIhiCD86+ cells (~89%).
source: Among those DQ+CD103+ migratory DCs, the vast majority of them were MHC IIhiCD86+ cells (∼89%) (Figure 6I), which indicated that these migratory DQ+CD103+DCs were indeed activated DCs.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6I.

claim: All migratory DQ+CD103+ DCs in DLN were DQ-Red− cells.
source: Consistent with the finding in the lungs, all these migratory DQ+CD103+ in DLN were DQ-Red− cells (Figure 6I).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6I.

claim: A portion of lung CD11B+DQ+ DCs were MHC IIhiCD86+ activated DCs.
source: Similar to CD103+DCs, we found that (1) a portion of lung CD11B+DQ+ DCs were MHC IIhiCD86+ activated DCs (Figure 6E)
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Activated DQ+CD11B+CD86+ DCs were all DQ-Red negative cells.
source: Similar to CD103+DCs, we found that (1) a portion of lung CD11B+DQ+ DCs were MHC IIhiCD86+ activated DCs (Figure 6E); (2) these activated DQ+CD11B+CD86+ DCs were all DQ-Red negative cells (Figure 6E)
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: All the DQ-Red−DC-Green+CD11B+ DCs were CD86+.
source: Similar to CD103+DCs, we found that (1) a portion of lung CD11B+DQ+ DCs were MHC IIhiCD86+ activated DCs (Figure 6E); (2) these activated DQ+CD11B+CD86+ DCs were all DQ-Red negative cells (Figure 6E); (3) all the DQ-Red−DC-Green+CD11B+ DCs were CD86+ (Figure 6E)
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Total CD11B+ DCs numbers were increased in DLN after CDG treatment.
source: Similar to CD103+DCs, we found that (1) a portion of lung CD11B+DQ+ DCs were MHC IIhiCD86+ activated DCs (Figure 6E); (2) these activated DQ+CD11B+CD86+ DCs were all DQ-Red negative cells (Figure 6E); (3) all the DQ-Red−DC-Green+CD11B+ DCs were CD86+ (Figure 6E); (4) total CD11B+ DCs numbers were increased in DLN (Figure 6J,L)
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figures 6J and 6L.

claim: Only a very small percentage of CD11B+ DCs (~0.8%) were DQ+ in DLN.
source: Similar to CD103+DCs, we found that (1) a portion of lung CD11B+DQ+ DCs were MHC IIhiCD86+ activated DCs (Figure 6E); (2) these activated DQ+CD11B+CD86+ DCs were all DQ-Red negative cells (Figure 6E); (3) all the DQ-Red−DC-Green+CD11B+ DCs were CD86+ (Figure 6E); (4) total CD11B+ DCs numbers were increased in DLN (Figure 6J,L); (5) only a very small percentage of these CD11B+ DCs (∼0.8%) were DQ+ (Figure 6J,M)
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figures 6J and 6M.

claim: The vast majority of DQ+CD11B+ migratory DC were MHC IIhiCD86+ cells (~82%).
source: Similar to CD103+DCs, we found that (1) a portion of lung CD11B+DQ+ DCs were MHC IIhiCD86+ activated DCs (Figure 6E); (2) these activated DQ+CD11B+CD86+ DCs were all DQ-Red negative cells (Figure 6E); (3) all the DQ-Red−DC-Green+CD11B+ DCs were CD86+ (Figure 6E); (4) total CD11B+ DCs numbers were increased in DLN (Figure 6J,L); (5) only a very small percentage of these CD11B+ DCs (∼0.8%) were DQ+ (Figure 6J,M); (6) the vast majority of DQ+CD11B+ migratory DC were MHC IIhiCD86+ cells (∼82%) (Figure 6K,N)
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figures 6K and 6N.

claim: All migratory DQ+CD11B+ DCs were DQ-Red− cells.
source: Similar to CD103+DCs, we found that (1) a portion of lung CD11B+DQ+ DCs were MHC IIhiCD86+ activated DCs (Figure 6E); (2) these activated DQ+CD11B+CD86+ DCs were all DQ-Red negative cells (Figure 6E); (3) all the DQ-Red−DC-Green+CD11B+ DCs were CD86+ (Figure 6E); (4) total CD11B+ DCs numbers were increased in DLN (Figure 6J,L); (5) only a very small percentage of these CD11B+ DCs (∼0.8%) were DQ+ (Figure 6J,M); (6) the vast majority of DQ+CD11B+ migratory DC were MHC IIhiCD86+ cells (∼82%) (Figure 6K,N); (7) all these migratory DQ+CD11B+ were DQ-Red− cells (Figure 6K).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6K.

claim: CDG only activated pinocytosis-efficient DCs in vivo.
source: The fact that these were the only CD86+ and DQ+ migratory DCs found in DLN after CDG treatment suggested that CDG only activated pinocytosis-efficient DCs in vivo.
evidence: Based on inference from the observation that only DQ-Red− (pinocytosis-efficient) DCs were CD86+ and migratory.

claim: It did not matter whether DCs were CD103+ or CD11B+ for CDG activation.
source: It did not matter whether they were CD103+ or CD11B+ DCs (Figure 6H,J).
evidence: Based on inference from similar activation patterns in both DC subsets.

claim: All the DQ-Green+DQ-Red+ cells were CD86− and non-migratory.
source: In contrast, all the DQ-Green+DQ-Red+ cells were CD86− and non-migratory, suggesting that though CDG enhanced Ag uptake in these cells (Figure 4), it did not lead to cell activation.
evidence: Based on inference from experimental observations about DQ-Red+ cells.

claim: Mucosal adjuvant activity of CDG requires MPYS in vivo.
source: Mucosal adjuvant activity of CDG requires MPYS in vivo (Blaauboer et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work by the authors (Blaauboer et al., 2014).

claim: Lung cells from Tmem173−/− mice had no increased OVA-647+ cells upon co-administration of OVA-647 and CDG.
source: Upon co-administration of OVA-647 and CDG, lung cells from Tmem173−/− mice had no increased OVA-647+ cells (Figure 7A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Tmem173−/− mice had significantly less CDG induced DQ-OVA+ cells than WT mice.
source: As expected, Tmem173−/− mice had significantly less CDG induced DQ-OVA+ cells than WT mice (Figure 7B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Both CD103+DC and CD11B+ DC from CDG treated Tmem173−/− mice had dramatically decreased DQ+ cells.
source: Both CD103+DC (Figure 7C) and CD11B+ DC (Figure 7D) from CDG treated Tmem173−/− mice, had dramatically decreased DQ+ cells (Figure 7E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figures 7C, 7D, and 7E.

claim: MPYS is critical for CDG induced DC Ag endocytosis and pinocytosis in vivo.
source: We concluded that MPYS is critical for CDG induced DC Ag endocytosis and pinocytosis in vivo.
evidence: Based on inference from the dramatic decrease in both DQ-Red+ and DQ-Red− cells in Tmem173−/− mice.

claim: No CD86+CD80+DQ+ MHC IIhi cells can be detected in CDG treated Tmem173−/− mice.
source: As expected, no CD86+CD80+DQ+ MHC IIhi cells can be detected in CDG treated Tmem173−/− mice (Figure 7F).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7F.

claim: CDG/PspA immunization significantly lowered the lung bacterial burden in WT mice.
source: CDG/PspA immunization significantly lowered the lung bacterial burden in the WT mice (Figure 7G).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7G.

claim: The bacterial burden in lungs from CDG/PspA and PspA immunized Tmem173−/− were not significantly different.
source: However, the bacterial burden in lungs from CDG/PspA and PspA immunized Tmem173−/− were not significantly different (Figure 7G).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7G.

claim: The mucosal pneumococcal vaccine adjuvant activity of CDG requires MPYS.
source: We concluded that the mucosal pneumococcal vaccine adjuvant activity of CDG requires MPYS.
evidence: Based on inference from the lack of protective immunity in Tmem173−/− mice.

claim: PspA immunized Tmem173−/− mice had significantly lower lung bacterial burden than PspA immunized WT mice.
source: Interestingly, PspA immunized Tmem173−/− mice had significantly lower lung bacterial burden than the PspA immunized WT mice (Figure 7G).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7G.

claim: Tmem173−/− mice are much more resistant to Streptococcus pneumoniae infection than WT mice.
source: We further found that Tmem173−/− mice, without PspA immunization, are much more resistant to Streptococcus pneumoniae infection than the WT mice (unpublished data).
evidence: Based on unpublished experimental observations by the authors.

claim: BALF cells from ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice had dramatically decreased MPYS expression (>90%).
source: BALF cells, which are overwhelmingly CD11Chi alveolar macrophages, had dramatically decreased MPYS expression (>90%) in ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice (Figure 8—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1B.

claim: MPYS expression in spleen B cells or T cells did not change in ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice.
source: MPYS expression in spleen B cells (IgD+) or T cells (CD4+ or CD8+) did not change in ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice (Figure 8—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1C.

claim: MPYS expression was dramatically decreased in both CD11C+MHC IIlow and CD11C+MHC IIhi populations in ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice.
source: MPYS expression was dramatically decreased in both populations in ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice (Figure 8—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1D.

claim: MPYS expression was eliminated in both CD103+ and CD11B+ DC subsets in ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice.
source: When we separated the DC population (CD11C+MHC IIhi) into CD103+ and CD11B+ DCs, we found that MPYS expression was eliminated in both DCs subsets (Figure 8—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The MPYS expression was down ~40% in MHC IIint CD11C− cells from ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice.
source: The MPYS expression was down ∼40% in MHC IIint CD11C− cells from ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice (Figure 8—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1D.

claim: NK cells showed ~40% decreased MPYS expression in ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice.
source: NK cells also showed ∼40% decreased MPYS expression in ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice (Figure 8—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1E.

claim: MPYS heterozygous mice had ~50% decreased MPYS expression.
source: MPYS heterozygous mice, which had ∼50% decreased MPYS expression (Figure 8—figure supplement 1F), were immunized with CDG and OVA.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1F.

claim: The total OVA-specific IgG production was similar in WT as in Tmem173+/− mice.
source: The total OVA-specific IgG production was similar in WT as in the Tmem173+/− mice (Figure 8—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1G.

claim: Partial decreased MPYS expression (~50%) does not affect CDG adjuvant activity.
source: Thus, the partial decreased MPYS expression (∼50%) does not affect CDG adjuvant activity.
evidence: Based on inference from similar IgG production in WT and Tmem173+/− mice.

claim: The total numbers of DQ+ cells were dramatically decreased in ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice.
source: The total numbers of DQ+ cells were dramatically decreased in ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice (Figure 8A,B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figures 8A and 8B.

claim: The decreased number of DQ+ cells was seen in both CD103+DC and CD11B+ DC from ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice.
source: The decreased number of DQ+ cells was seen in both CD103+DC (Figure 8C,D) and CD11B+ DC (Figure 8C,E) from ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figures 8C, 8D, and 8E.

claim: The numbers of decreased DQ+ DCs in ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice was comparable to that of Tmem173−/− mice.
source: The numbers of decreased DQ+ DCs in ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox/flox was comparable to that of Tmem173−/− mice (Figure 8B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: CDG induced DC Ag uptake requires MPYS expression in CD11C+ cells.
source: Thus, CDG induced DC Ag uptake requires MPYS expression in CD11C+ cells.
evidence: Based on inference from the dramatic decrease in DQ+ cells in ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice.

claim: CDG induced TH1 polarizing cytokines IL-12p70 and IFNγ were significantly decreased in ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice.
source: CDG induced TH1 polarizing (IL-12p70 and IFNγ) and TH17 polarizing (IL-23 and IL-6) cytokines were significantly decreased in ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice (Figure 8F,H).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figures 8F and 8H.

claim: CDG induced TH17 polarizing cytokines IL-23 and IL-6 were significantly decreased in ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice.
source: CDG induced TH1 polarizing (IL-12p70 and IFNγ) and TH17 polarizing (IL-23 and IL-6) cytokines were significantly decreased in ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice (Figure 8F,H).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figures 8F and 8H.

claim: There was not much decrease in TH2 polarizing cytokines IL-5 and IL-13 in ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice.
source: Surprisingly, we did not see much of a decrease in the TH2 polarizing cytokines (IL-5, IL-13) (Figure 8G).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8G.

claim: MPYS expression in CD11C+ cells is critical for TH1 and TH17 polarizing cytokine production in vivo.
source: Thus, MPYS expression in CD11C+ cells is critical for TH1 and TH17 polarizing cytokine production in vivo.
evidence: Based on inference from the significant decrease in TH1 and TH17 cytokines in ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice.

claim: CDG induced IFN-λ, IL-22, TNF-α, and IL-1β productions were dramatically decreased in ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice.
source: CDG induced IFN-λ, IL-22, TNF-α, and IL-1β productions were also dramatically decreased in ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice (Figure 8I,J).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figures 8I and 8J.

claim: DCs expression of MPYS was critical for the generation of TH1 and TH17 polarizing cytokine during intranasal administration of CDG.
source: Since the CD11C+MHC IIhi DCs were the only activated CD11C+ cells by CDG in vivo (Figures 4E, 5E), we concluded that DCs expression of MPYS was critical for the generation of TH1 and TH17 polarizing cytokine during intranasal administration of CDG.
evidence: Based on inference from the observation that only MHC IIhi DCs were activated and the cytokine decrease in ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice.

claim: The lung epithelial cytokine TSLP was slightly lower in CDG treated ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice than in Tmem173Flox/Flox mice, but it was not statistically significant.
source: The lung epithelial cytokine TSLP was slightly lower in CDG treated ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice than in the Tmem173Flox/Flox mice, but it was not statistically significant (Figure 8K).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8K.

claim: The lung epithelial cytokine IL-33 production was significantly lower in CDG treated ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice than in Tmem173Flox/Flox.
source: However, the lung epithelial cytokine IL-33 production was significantly lower in CDG treated ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice than in the Tmem173Flox/Flox (Figure 8K).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8K.

claim: There is a crosstalk/communication between lung epithelial cells and CD11C+ cells during CDG induced immune response.
source: We favored the idea that there is a crosstalk/communication between lung epithelial cells and CD11C+ cells during CDG induced immune response.
evidence: Based on speculation from the observation that epithelial cytokine IL-33 was affected by MPYS deletion in CD11C+ cells.

claim: ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice exhibited significantly decreased production of anti-OVA IgG1, IgG2C, and nasal IgA.
source: ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice exhibited significantly decreased production of anti-OVA IgG1, IgG2C, and nasal IgA (Figure 9A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9A.

claim: CDG/OVA immunized ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice still generated decent amounts of anti-OVA Ab.
source: Noticeably different from the Tmem173−/− mice, where no anti-OVA Ab could be detected, CDG/OVA immunized ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice still generated decent amounts of anti-OVA Ab (Figure 9A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9A.

claim: ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice showed decreased anti-PspA IgG1, IgG2C, and nasal IgA production in comparison to immunized WT mice.
source: Again, ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice showed decreased anti-PspA IgG1, IgG2C, and nasal IgA production in comparison to the immunized WT mice (Figure 9B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9B.

claim: ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice still had elevated anti-PspA Ab responses compared to MPYS−/− mice.
source: Similar to the CDG/OVA immunization, ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice still had elevated anti-PspA Ab responses compared to the MPYS−/− mice (Figure 9B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9B.

claim: CDG/PspA immunized ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice showed dramatically decreased TH1, TH2, and TH17 responses in the ex vivo recall assay on splenocytes.
source: The CDG/PspA immunized ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice also showed dramatically decreased TH1, TH2, and TH17 responses in the ex vivo recall assay on splenocytes (Figure 9C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9C.

claim: TH1, TH17 and, to a lesser degree, TH2 responses were decreased in lung cells from ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice.
source: Similar to the responses in splenocytes, TH1, TH17 and, to a lesser degree, TH2 responses were decreased in lung cells from ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice (Figure 9D).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9D.

claim: CDG/PspA immunization significantly lowered the lung bacterial burden in Tmem173Flox/Flox mice.
source: While CDG/PspA immunization significantly lowered the lung bacterial burden in the Tmem173Flox/Flox mice, it did not alter the bacterial burden from lungs of the ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice (Figure 9E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9E.

claim: CDG/PspA immunization did not alter the bacterial burden from lungs of ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice.
source: While CDG/PspA immunization significantly lowered the lung bacterial burden in the Tmem173Flox/Flox mice, it did not alter the bacterial burden from lungs of the ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice (Figure 9E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9E.

claim: The mucosal pneumococcal vaccine adjuvant activity of CDG requires MPYS expression in CD11C+ cells.
source: We concluded that the mucosal pneumococcal vaccine adjuvant activity of CDG requires MPYS expression in CD11C+ cells.
evidence: Based on inference from the lack of protective immunity in ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice.

claim: PspA immunized Tmem173Flox/Flox and ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice had similar lung bacterial burden.
source: Noticeably, unlike the Tmem173−/− mice, PspA immunized Tmem173Flox/Flox and ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice had similar lung bacterial burden (Figure 9E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9E.

claim: CDG/PspA immunized ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice had a severe defect in anti-PspA Ab production compared to immunized ItgaxCre-C57BL/6 mice.
source: Similar to the observation in Figure 9, CDG/PspA immunized ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice had a severe defect in anti-PspA Ab production compared to immunized ItgaxCre-C57BL/6 mice (Figure 9—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1A.

claim: TH responses in spleen cells from ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice were largely non existent, except for IL-5.
source: Their TH responses in spleen cells were largely non existent, except for IL-5 (Figure 9—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1B.

claim: CDG enhances Ag uptake in APCs and non-APCs in vivo.
source: Our study revealed two novel in vivo mechanisms of action of the mucosal vaccine adjuvant CDG (Figure 10). First, CDG enhances Ag uptake in APCs and non-APCs in vivo.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing increased OVA-647+ cells in both MHC II+ and MHC II− populations.

claim: CDG activates pinocytosis-efficient cells in vivo.
source: Our study revealed two novel in vivo mechanisms of action of the mucosal vaccine adjuvant CDG (Figure 10). First, CDG enhances Ag uptake in APCs and non-APCs in vivo. Second, CDG activates pinocytosis-efficient cells in vivo.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing selective activation of DQ-Red− (pinocytosis-efficient) DCs.

claim: Only cells that efficiently take up CDG via pinocytosis will be activated.
source: Thus, though intranasally administered CDG enhances Ag uptake in all types of cells, only cells that efficiently take up CDG, via pinocytosis, will be activated (Figure 10A).
evidence: Based on inference from CDG's inability to cross membranes and selective activation of pinocytosis-efficient cells.

claim: CDG enhances MPYS-dependent Ag uptake in cells directly taking up CDG.
source: We propose that CDG enhances MPYS-dependent Ag uptake in cells directly taking up CDG (pinocytosis-efficient, OVA-647Low, DQ-Green+DQ-Red− cells).
evidence: Based on speculation from experimental observations about selective activation and MPYS dependence.

claim: In cells that do not take up CDG, Ag uptake is enhanced by the cytokine milieu generated mainly by CDG activated CD11C+ cells.
source: In cells that do not take up CDG (OVA-647hi, DQ-Green+DQ-Red+ cells), Ag uptake is enhanced by the cytokine milieu generated mainly by CDG activated CD11C+ cells (Figure 10B).
evidence: Based on speculation from experimental observations about enhanced Ag uptake in non-activated cells and cytokine production.

claim: Intranasally administered CDG directly primed pulmonary DCs, leading to MPYS-dependent production of TH polarizing cytokines in vivo.
source: We favored the hypothesis that intranasally administered CDG directly primed pulmonary DCs, leading to MPYS-dependent production of TH polarizing cytokines in vivo (Figure 10C).
evidence: Based on speculation supported by detection of IL-12 and IFNγ producing DCs and decreased cytokines in ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice.

claim: The deletion of MPYS in MHC IIhiCD11C+ cells (DCs) was responsible for the impaired TH1 and TH17 polarizing cytokine production in vivo.
source: This suggested that the deletion of MPYS in MHC IIhiCD11C+ cells (DCs) was responsible for the impaired TH1 and TH17 polarizing cytokine production in vivo.
evidence: Based on inference from the observation that only MHC IIhiCD11C+ cells were activated and cytokines decreased in ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice.

claim: Besides DCs, MPYS expression in other cells contributes to the adjuvant activity of CDG in vivo.
source: Therefore besides DCs, MPYS expression in other cells contributes to the adjuvant activity of CDG in vivo.
evidence: Based on inference from the observation that ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice still have some Ab and TH responses.

claim: The OVA-647+CD11C−MHC IIint APC was activated by CDG in vivo.
source: We found that the OVA-647+CD11C−MHC IIint APC was activated by CDG in vivo (Figure 4E).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: CD11C− OVA-647+ MHC IIint CD86+ cells may contribute to the adjuvant activity of CDG in ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice.
source: Thus, these CD11C− OVA-647+ MHC IIint CD86+ cells may contribute to the adjuvant activity of CDG in ItgaxCreTmem173Flox/Flox mice.
evidence: Based on speculation from the observation that these cells are activated and not affected by CD11C-specific MPYS deletion.

claim: CDG activated NLRP3 inflammasome independent of STING/MPYS.
source: A previous study showed that CDG activated NLRP3 inflammasome independent of STING/MPYS (Abdul-Sater et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Abdul-Sater et al., 2013 study.

claim: CDG bound to hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated channel 4 (HCN4) and inhibited cAMP regulated heart rate.
source: CDG also bound to hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated channel 4 (HCN4) and inhibited cAMP regulated heart rate (Lolicato et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Lolicato et al., 2014 study.

claim: Cyclic di-AMP induces human monocyte apoptosis independent of STING/MPYS.
source: Very recently, it was found that cyclic di-AMP, a similar cyclic dinucleotide for STING/MPYS, induces human monocyte apoptosis independent of STING/MPYS (Tosolini et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Tosolini et al., 2015 study.

claim: Other mammalian receptors for CDG exist.
source: Thus, other mammalian receptors for CDG exist.
evidence: Based on inference from the observation of MPYS-independent effects and citations to studies showing alternative CDG targets.

claim: 2′3′-cGAMP can be hydrolyzed by the ecto-nucleotide phosphodiesterase (ENPP1) found in mammalian cells.
source: As a mammalian cyclic dinucleotide, 2′3′-cGAMP can be hydrolyzed by the ecto-nucleotide phosphodiesterase (ENPP1) found in mammalian cells (Li et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Li et al., 2014 study.

claim: As a bacterial cyclic dinucleotide, CDG may be more resistant to hydrolysis when introduced into mammalian cells.
source: On the contrary, as a bacterial cyclic dinucleotide, CDG may be more resistant to hydrolysis when introduced into mammalian cells.
evidence: Based on speculation from the difference between bacterial and mammalian cyclic dinucleotides.

claim: The anti-tumor molecules CMA and DMXAA activate mouse, but not human MPYS signaling.
source: The anti-tumor molecules 10-carboxymethyl-9-acridanone (CMA) (Cavlar et al., 2013) and 5,6-dimethylxanthenone-4-acetic acid (DMXAA) (Conlon et al., 2013) activate mouse, but not, human MPYS signaling.
evidence: Supported by citations to Cavlar et al., 2013 and Conlon et al., 2013 studies.

claim: CDG is functional in human cells.
source: CDG, on the other hand, is functional in human cells as well (Karaolis et al., 2007; Yi et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to Karaolis et al., 2007 and Yi et al., 2013 studies.

claim: CDG binds to mouse MPYS/STING and human MPYS/STING with similar dissociation constant (Kd: 2–5 μM).
source: In fact, CDG binds to mouse MPYS/STING (Burdette et al., 2011) and human MPYS/STING (Ouyang et al., 2012; Shang et al., 2012; Shu et al., 2012; Yin et al., 2012) with similar dissociation constant (Kd: 2–5 μM).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies (Burdette et al., 2011; Ouyang et al., 2012; Shang et al., 2012; Shu et al., 2012; Yin et al., 2012).

claim: Human TMEM173 gene displays great heterogeneity.
source: Nevertheless, we first discovered that human TMEM173 gene displays great heterogeneity (Jin et al., 2011b).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work by the authors (Jin et al., 2011b).

claim: A loss-of-function human TMEM173 variant HAQ (R71H-G230A-R293Q) is carried by ~20% of Americans.
source: We further identified a loss-of-function human TMEM173 variant HAQ (R71H-G230A-R293Q) that is carried by ∼20% of Americans (Jin et al., 2011b).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work by the authors (Jin et al., 2011b).

claim: Many human TMEM173 variants are functionally different from the R232 (wild type) TMEM173 allele.
source: In vitro studies demonstrated that many of these human TMEM173 variants are functionally different from the R232 (wild type) TMEM173 allele (Ablasser et al., 2013; Gao et al., 2013b; Yi et al., 2013; Zhang et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies (Ablasser et al., 2013; Gao et al., 2013b; Yi et al., 2013; Zhang et al., 2013).
